title: Dispute procedure and settlement
summary: Local case records and a narrow signed debt-release mechanism are implemented. Future Goals propose an agreed dispute procedure, symmetric evidence access, authorized consequences and payment handling; their policy and implementation steps remain to be defined.

goals.title: Retain inspectable local dispute records
goals.description: The companion retains supplied case history, attributed evidence and challenges for analysis. Its shared-manifest checks do not establish a hosted symmetric evidence-access service, complete history, privacy-preserving scrutiny package or accepted dispute procedure. Analysis remains ANALYSIS_ONLY, with financial authority NONE and settlement policy UNSPECIFIED; workflow integration does not establish reliable reasoning.

milestones.title: Verify local case evidence, revisions and attributed challenges
milestones.description: Implemented local record component, supported by synthetic regression tests and the recorded 2 October container validation. Contract-bound cases retain a supplied-history frontier and hash-linked revisions; signed submissions and challenges attribute content without establishing its truth or changing core rights. The case envelope is unsigned and has only OPEN and UNDER_REVIEW states. The core's separate signed DisputeOpened event is not a dedicated authenticated opening/notice binding for the companion case. No general closure, escalation or settlement follows from analysis readiness.
acceptance: Case inspection binds the supplied Contract, trust, context, scope and local frontier without claiming global history completeness.

Requester and Operator submissions bind exact original bytes; altered content, fabricated sources and an audience excluding a party are rejected for analysis without changing the independently verified core projection.
Hash-linked revisions preserve retained evidence and identify earlier results as stale; signed challenges retain attributed references and history without reversing contractual rights.
Original evidence, untrusted extraction, supplied sensor claims and explicit redaction or omission retain distinct meanings; signatures establish authorship rather than physical truth.

goals.title: Apply only explicitly authorized settlement effects
goals.description: The core supports an exact R/O-authorized release of existing debt units independently of the analysis companion. Authored lifecycle and research notes propose mutual review, preserved rights and a pre-agreed procedure after failed negotiation; they adopt no general escalation mechanism, fallback allocation, remedy, case-closure rule or new resolver authority. Payment and payee receipt remain separate from any authorized release.

milestones.title: Verify policy-limited bilateral compensation and expense releases
milestones.description: Implemented core protocol component with synthetic validation, not an automatic settlement service or a real payment result. When the signed policy enables bilateral_balance_releases, BILATERAL_SETTLEMENT requires independent R/O authorization of the exact proposal and releases specified existing R-to-O compensation or expense units. It cannot create a new payment obligation, refund, general Contract patch or protection-claim release, or change M's rights. Release coverage is irrevocable within this action model; a scoped release does not close the entire dispute. The companion does not construct or submit the action, and model outputs supply no settlement authority.
acceptance: The verifier requires the signed enabling policy, exact Requester and Operator authorizations, an existing eligible obligation, entitlement certificates and matching allocated units and monetary basis.
Synthetic lifecycle checks show that a scoped release reduces only the specified R-to-O balance while preserving M's separate rights; unsupported releases of M's service fee are rejected.
Receipt coverage and release coverage remain separately visible, with overlapping debt units counted once in the outstanding balance.
Analysis, mediation recommendations and assurance assessments create no release authority; the release action itself transfers no funds and creates no payee-signed receipt.

goals.title: Define dispute opening, notice, claims and responses
goals.description: Proposed scope: define how either party raises a scoped claim, how the companion case refers to the exact authenticated opening event and any notice evidence, and how responses, contested facts and later additions remain attributable. Decide notice requirements, response expectations and treatment of silence, technical failure and missing material without treating them as consent or proof of fault. Notification delivery, reading, sufficient dispute notice, acknowledgment and consent remain distinct; durable storage establishes none of these by itself. Define the interface with Identity's silent clock-out/sign-out policy without resuming sensing or work. Existing obligations retain their own rules. Assignments and APK buildout supply participant review; Durable infrastructure supplies transport/recovery semantics and Server side services retains exact opening and notice records under this Hero's procedural meanings. No opening-to-notice binding, response timetable or service responsibility is adopted here.

goals.title: Provide symmetric evidence contribution, access and scrutiny
goals.description: Proposed scope: let both parties contribute contemporaneous evidence and inspect relevant case material, preserving attributed originals and later additions. Define missing, contested, omitted or redacted material and a scrutiny package at each supplied-history frontier, without claiming complete global history. Distinguish an absent record, an unsigned failure, a signed failure claim and separate composed-sensor outcomes; these do not alone establish no attempt, physical effort, fault or entitlement. Sensors supplies original request/context, applicable profile or metric versions, outcomes and uncertainty; artifact integrity, task usability and responsibility remain distinct judgments. Use shared case/evidence interfaces with domain-specific dispute and incident views rather than duplicate case systems. Material incidents and insurance supplies incident preservation needs, recipients and purposes; urgent assistance and preservation must not await final classification or ordinary dispute resolution. Scrutiny does not authorize underwriting reuse. Identity supplies principal/key authority and identity-data custody/access policy; private registration and authentication media must not enter routine evidence merely because stored. Durable infrastructure supplies authenticated references/exchange semantics and Server side services enforces recipient access and retention. Package contents, disclosure and privacy remain decisions; local plaintext replay establishes no production service.

goals.title: Support exact mutual settlement and explicit closure scope
goals.description: Proposed scope: develop the authored negotiation design into reviewable proposals with distinct revisions and content digests, stated consequences, remaining claims and independent authorization of the same exact supported resolution by Requester and Operator. Silence, inactivity and refusal must not substitute for consent; partial settlement preserves unrelated rights and M's rights and identifies harm claims outside its scope. Decide closure, finality and possible reopening while retaining the existing release action's irrevocability; revising a proposal does not revoke an older signature. Assignments and APK buildout provide review that distinguishes a local acknowledgment, exact signed proposal, verified effect, payment, case closure and safe resumption of physical work. Durable infrastructure supplies retry/status semantics without re-signing, withdrawing or reversing effects; Server side services retains exact records under this Hero's meanings. Case closure cannot substitute for an applicable work-change/amendment path or erase accrued rights. No general closure certificate, signature-withdrawal mechanism or new settlement effect is selected here.

goals.title: Define challenges, escalation and inconclusive outcomes
goals.description: Proposed scope: specify the procedure participants would authorize before cooperation when negotiation does not produce mutual agreement. Decide scope, decision authority, challenges/review, missing or inconclusive evidence and the economic consequences of delay or unresolved claims. The working direction favors the accepted ordinary payment procedure with external scrutiny; it selects no routine opt-out, adjudicator, deadline, fallback allocation or automatic closure. This Hero supplies proposed procedural and consent meanings; Governance and launch readiness frames the actual provider/resolver's accountability, selected-jurisdiction safeguards and review/adoption for the chosen offering. The approving person or institution remains unselected, and institutional formation or launch approval cannot itself create a missing contractual power. Material incidents and insurance owns incident classification, response and external-process requirements. An incident notice, referral or insurer communication alone is not a payment instruction, settlement, liability determination or closure authority.

goals.title: Define authorized remedies and explicit payment consequences
goals.description: Proposed scope: define how an accepted procedure could connect supported facts, uncertainty, Contract clauses and participant declarations to an explained, bounded consequence, including an exact amount or percentage and monetary basis when payment is in scope. Decide permitted effects and required authority for disputed time/scope, extra work, cancellation, partial completion and expenses, preserving protected and unrelated rights. The Operators union supplies reviewed collective policy versions, calculation inputs and auditable remuneration calculations; Assignments binds and presents accepted Contract terms. Preserve original claims, approved/disputed inputs, authority references and policy versions so correcting an input remains distinguishable from authorizing a new contractual effect. A later vote, rate change or recalculation cannot silently replace accepted terms; valid arithmetic, evidence acceptance or completion acknowledgment does not itself authorize a ballot or payment. Priors owns reliable interpretation and prior influence; this Hero defines consent/consequences with Governance review. Neither an analysis nor two signatures authorizes an unsupported effect. The implemented bilateral release retains its narrow scope; no new award formula, refund, extra-work obligation, penalty, default split or model authority is adopted here.

goals.title: Connect authorized outcomes to separate payment and receipt records
goals.description: Proposed scope: define the handoff from a valid contractual outcome to separately authorized external payment, payment observation and payee receipt, preserving exact obligations, released units, paid units and remaining balances. Preserve the recorded requester-funded direction, direct Requester-to-Operator task payment and no commission or deduction from Operator compensation; a dispute proposal does not adopt a provider or custody arrangement. Decide responsibilities and records for payment failure, disputed payment claims and reconciliation without inferring transfer or discharge from an analysis result, release, delivery acknowledgment or case-closure label. This Hero defines procedural authority and outcome meanings, Server side services implements any separately authorized provider handoff, Governance reviews the selected arrangement, and participant interfaces explain the states. No provider, custody model, transfer authority or real payment capability is selected or implemented here.

goals.title: Evaluate procedure fairness, usability and resistance to gaming
goals.description: Proposed scope: develop a review and evaluation approach for the dispute procedure across both roles, considering comprehension, evidence access, selective presentation, delay, uncertain outcomes, already performed labor and retained funds. Examine false accusations, technical failures, accessibility and any proposed observation challenges or deterrents without equating a lost dispute or missed challenge with deception. Decide what evidence could justify claims about speed, impartiality, proportionality or useful deterrence before adopting rules or thresholds. This Hero validates procedure and supported-consequence requirements; Priors owns reasoning evaluation, Sensors physical evidence, Identity authority/privacy policy, Assignments participant comprehension and exact consent, Durable infrastructure workflow conformance, APK native behavior and Server side services hosted transactions/access/retention. Material incidents and insurance supplies incident-specific validation; Governance frames independent review and adoption. Any joint outcome needs one primary Hero, named contributors, defined handoffs and shared acceptance evidence with each scoped result recorded once. Component checks establish no end-to-end, physical, deployment or institutional acceptance. Time, useful-compute and hybrid deterrents remain research candidates with unresolved triggers, calibration and authority; no evaluation plan, performance target or enforcement rule is committed here.
